population.span: The multicenter, double-blind, randomized PHILO trial compared the safety and efficacy of ticagrelor vs. clopidogrel in 801 patients with ACS (Japanese, n=721; Taiwanese, n=35; South Korean, n=44; unknown ethnicity, n=1). All were planned to undergo percutaneous coronary intervention and randomized within 24 h of symptom onset.

endpoint.span: Primary safety and efficacy endpoints were time to first occurrence of any major bleeding event and to any event from the composite of myocardial infarction, stroke or death from vascular causes, respectively.

estimate.span: the composite primary efficacy endpoint occurred in 9.0% and in 6.3% of ticagrelor- and clopidogrel-treated patients, respectively (HR, 1.47; 95% CI: 0.88-2.44).

ci.span: the composite primary efficacy endpoint occurred in 9.0% and in 6.3% of ticagrelor- and clopidogrel-treated patients, respectively (HR, 1.47; 95% CI: 0.88-2.44).

served_mismatch: The served HR and confidence interval match the abstract and registry for the requested composite endpoint. However, the served intention-to-treat label is not established: the registry specifies a Full Analysis set restricted to randomized patients with available post-randomization efficacy data. The fulltext_verified provenance is unsupported by this packet, which holds abstracts and a registry record only.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The entry population comprised patients with ACS planned for PCI; registry eligibility specifies a minimum age of 20 years, consistent with the adult ACS question.

notes: Registry spans supply the analysis set, treatment doses and endpoint-specific follow-up. The analysis-set wording also occurs for another efficacy endpoint, but the bound occurrence is under RESULT OUTCOME 1. The registry title states low-dose ASA background therapy in both arms.
